newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS- KLM shares ride high on merger speculation.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS- KLM shares ride high on merger speculation.

text.p: Shares in Dutch carrier KLM soared to a new all-time high in Amsterdam on Wednesday as reports it was in talks to sell its 19 percent stake in U.S. partner Northwest rekindled merger speculation.
KLM confirmed that the sale of its Northwest shares was one of the options open to it in resolving the partners' long-running feud over KLM's say in the U.S. carrier.
"One of the options is a possible sale of shares to Northwest," KLM spokesman Peter Wellhuener said. "How important (an option) it is, we will not comment."
Analysts hailed the news as a positive development, saying a share sell-off was not at all unlikely and represented "an ideal way" to further the KLM-Northwest alliance.

But dealers on the Amsterdam bourse said the jump in KLM's share price to a new all-time high of 63.50 guilders was prompted by investor speculation it could be preparing to get into bed with British Airways and American.
"Any news on KLM's link-up with Northwest sparks this kind of share reaction," one said. "Investors have never quite given up on a deal with British Airways."
The two airlines' respective U.S. partnerships have been seen as the major stumbling block to an Anglo-Dutch link-up.
British Airways' planned partnership with American -- currently awaiting approval from Brussels -- would mean KLM having to give up Northwest if it wanted to team up with BA.
Talks on an alliance between KLM and BA were broken off at an advanced stage in 1992 after KLM objected to the amount of control it would be afforded under a prospective partnership.
However, analysts were quick to quash the idea of a British Airways link, saying a Northwest share sell-off was more likely to signal closer ties between the two squabbling partners than a divorce.
"Lufthansa has shown you don't need cross- shareholdings to pursue a successful partnership," said Richard Brakenhoff, airlines analyst with MeesPierson.

"This would be an ideal way of furthering the partnership ...once the conflict is resolved the two could extend the length of their contracts from one to six years and significantly enhance the synergy benefits," he said.
Until now the lucrative alliance between the two airlines, under which they operate as a single carrier on transatlantic routes, has been based on short-term contracts.
The two carriers have been locked in a long-running dispute over KLM's rights to a further five percent Northwest stake under an option exercisable in 1998.
KLM is currently suing Northwest over a shareholder rights plan capping its holding at current levels. Northwest in turn has accused KLM of being out to gain control.

Outgoing KLM president Pieter Bouw told a news conference in May the Dutch carrier was in talks to resolve their boardroom battle, adding he hoped to announce a positive outcome within the foreseeable future.
But he declined then to comment on speculation KLM was prepared to sell its Northwest stake in return for a multi-year partnership agreement.
Wellhuener said on Wednesday that management talks between the two partners were ongoing, but declined to comment on their progress.
"I cannot say...KLM will not comment on the talks until their outcome," Wellhuener said.
KLM shares were trading up 2.30 guilders or 3.8 percent at 62.60 guilders at 1028 GMT, outpacing a rise of 0.44 percent on the AEX blue chip index.
